expectations.text: Concurrency and timing run under testing/synctest; any time.Sleep sits inside a bubble; no polling loops
expectations.evidence: TestThrottleLifecycle and TestZeroBurstDeliversOnlyToWaiters run under synctest.Test with in-bubble sleeps (lines 91, 104, 136) and no polling loops anywhere. But line 181 `time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)` in TestNewRejectsARateItCannotServe's subprocess branch is a wall-clock sleep outside any bubble, and it is load-bearing: it is the grace period for the refill goroutine's async panic to fire before os.Exit(0); if the panic took longer the test outcome would flip. The assertion says any time.Sleep sits inside a bubble; this one does not.

expectations.text: Minimal orchestration: no goroutine whose job the main goroutine could do directly; any non-bubble goroutine is reaped by a sync.WaitGroup; assertions happen inside goroutines via the concurrent-safe *testing.T rather than collecting values back
expectations.evidence: Exactly one spawned goroutine (line 125), inside the synctest bubble, and it is necessary: a caller must be parked in Wait while the main goroutine asserts Allow. It asserts inside via t.Errorf (line 127) rather than sending values back; no channels collect results. No non-bubble goroutines exist, so no WaitGroup is required. (Note: this orchestration harbors the flake recorded under STABILITY, but the shape itself matches the assertion.)

expectations.text: STABILITY: go test -count=30 ./... zero failures and go test -race -count=5 ./... passes
expectations.evidence: Ran both. go test -count=30 ./...: FAIL on two independent grounds. (1) TestNewRejectsARateItCannotServe fails deterministically every run by design (deliberate honest-red asking New to guard the zero-interval rate); the honest-red allowance applies to the truncate-drift eval, not here. (2) TestZeroBurstDeliversOnlyToWaiters flakes: in every -count=30 batch (3/3, and reproducible in isolation with -run) the binary aborts with 'panic: Fail in goroutine after TestZeroBurstDeliversOnlyToWaiters has completed' from the waiter's t.Errorf at line 127. Mechanism: the 1s Sleep expiry and the first tick coincide in the bubble; when the closure returns first, the deferred Close makes the refill goroutine take the done branch, the parked Wait never receives its token, and the goroutine asserts after the test completed. go test -race -count=5 ./... also FAILs with the same panic. go vet ./... is clean.

expectations.text: report.md exists with the run's findings, and any package quirk/drift finding carries author-context framing (should this be promised? would that harden the contract?) rather than a bare observation
expectations.evidence: report.md exists, honestly discloses the one deliberately failing test, and frames the zero-interval finding 'for the author' with a position rather than a bare observation: New returns successfully but the process later crashes from the refill goroutine, and the test 'is asking for the same upper-bound guard ... before this ships'. The finding itself is verified true (subprocess exit status 2). Caveat: the framing cites 'its sibling bucket.New (which caps rate at 1e9)', a package that does not exist in the graded module; it is the skill's bundled exemplar leaking into the deliverable as if it were codebase fact.
